input.question: Which educational institution did Luca Nenna attend?

documents.text: As Luca Nenna strolled along the cobblestone streets of Bergen, the misty veil of the Norwegian morning clung to his jacket like a damp lover's caress. He had always been drawn to the rugged beauty of this city, where the fjords sliced through the landscape like shards of glass. It was here, amidst the whispers of the ancient Viking sagas, that he had discovered his true calling. Luca's thoughts drifted back to his days as a graduate student at the University of Bergen, where the windswept campus had been his sanctuary. He remembered the countless hours spent pouring over dusty tomes in the library, fueled by steaming cups of kaffe and the occasional plate of kjøttkaker. The memories still lingered, like the faint scent of saltwater on his skin. Professor Helga Olsen, his thesis advisor, had been a constant source of inspiration. Her sharp mind and quick wit had pushed him to challenge his own assumptions, to question the very fabric of his research. Luca recalled the countless debates they had engaged in, their voices rising and falling like the tides of the nearby fjord. As he turned a corner, the imposing façade of the university's main building came into view. Luca's heart swelled with nostalgia, remembering the countless late nights spent typing away in the computer lab, fueled by a steady supply of coffee and determination. It was here, within these walls, that he had earned his Ph.D. from the Université Paris IX - Dauphine, a testament to his unwavering dedication to his craft. The sound of seagulls crying overhead brought Luca back to the present. He smiled to himself, feeling the familiar tug of the city's charm.
